sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Turbine-Driven Critical Care Invasive Ventilators

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law heritage with strong Common Law influence in commercial and trust/foundation practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Various Double Taxation Agreements (DTAAs) incl. Korea, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Qatar, Spain, United Arab Emirates

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995, Article 21 (Private Interest Foundations); Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015 (AML/CFT regime for non-financial sectors); Executive Decree No. 635 of 2018 and amendments; Resolution of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) adopting FATF Recommendations; Legislative Decree No. 2 of 2016 (Legal Persons and Beneficial Ownership Reporting); Supreme Court ruling of 27 March 2019 (declared Article 4 of Decree 363 upholding beneficial ownership register access); Unified Text of Law 2 of 2011 and its amendments (AML/CFT with asset laundering provisions). Beneficial ownership data is filed with the General Directorate of Revenues (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access_With_Confidential_Details_Reserved (Registered agents must disclose UBO to regulators; not freely public; PIF founders and beneficiaries are confidential by law, unless a criminal/AML inquiry or competent court order requires disclosure).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Characters of the Founder (if an entity) and Certified Copy of Articles of Foundation (Draft/Bylaws)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Notary Public/Notary of the Republic of Panama or Consular officer in the country of origin for foreign-issued instruments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for signatures executed in countries party to the 1961 Hague Convention) OR Consular Legalization at a Panama Consulate if origin is a non-Hague member (e.g., certain Middle East jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Founder or Corporate Parent (if corporate founder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original Company Registry Chamber or Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization (depending on issuing country status in the Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Beneficial Owner Declaration Form (Formulario de Declaración de Beneficiario Final), including each UBO with direct or indirect participation >= 25%, signed before a Panamanian Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama; form template provided by DGI
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification only; no apostille if notarized in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport/Valid Government ID of each UBO, founder, and if applicable, officers, or testigos (witnesses)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport/ID authority of the home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy in home country then Apostille/Consular Legalization; or executed before a Panamanian Notary with original ID

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (if incorporator or legal representative is acting on behalf of founder/UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the issuing jurisdiction, registered in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Reference Letter from a regulated financial institution serving as insurance underwriter confirmation for medical device manufacturer liability if required by due diligence officer (provided to registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank or insurance company in the operating jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mail or secure courier; no apostille required unless internal policy demands; may require notarization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, council members, and the Foundation Guardian (if natural person) against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions, Panama's List of Threatening Persons (Judge for risks of terrorist financing, extortion, and money laundering per Resolución 006-2018 UAF), and local Panamanian PEP lists. Also screen against World Bank/UNCAC corruption lists due to government LC procurement element. Enhanced due diligence required when a UBO is a PEP (foreign, domestic, or international organization PEP). SDN-listed individuals or entities cannot be appointed as Foundation Guardian or beneficiary without prior OFAC specific license. Reasonable suspicion of UBO identity concealment triggers suspicious transaction report to UAF within 48 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), via the online platform 'Reporte Electrónico de Nombre o Razon Social' – official portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be in any language using the Latin script; if using non-Latin script (e.g., Arabic, Hebrew), an approved phonetic transliteration into Spanish or English is mandatory. The name must end with 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Private Interest Foundation' or accepted abbreviation 'FIP' in the Spanish version. No name may be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity; the Registry also prohibits names that render the purpose illegal or contrary to Panamanian public order. For names in Spanish, accentuation rules and limited punctuation (periods, commas, hyphens) are allowed but must not imply governmental affiliation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bank, Savings Bank (unless prior Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá authorization)
Seguros, Insurance, Reinsurance (requires Superintendencia de Seguros prior authorization)
Trust, Fideicomiso, Valle, Valle de la (in combination with 'Trust' requires relevant license)
Bolsa, Exchange, Securities (requires Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores authorization)
Fundación de Interés Privado (only permitted after the name as suffix, cannot be used as part of the distinctive token)
Panamá, República de Panamá, Gobierno, Presidencia, Ministerio, Municipalidad, Autoridad, Estado (if implying official Panamanian sponsorship)
International, Mundial, Global (when used to imply intergovernmental status)
United Nations, ONU, UN, UNESCO, WHO, OMS, Organization of American States, OAS (without permission from such international bodies)
Médico, Hospital, Clínica (when appearing in the name, may render requirement for Ministry of Health license for medical device commercialization)
Socialista, Comunista, Nazi, Fascista, or other political/ideological terms deemed offensive under Decency norms
Error, Ltd., Limited, Inc., S.A., LLC, or any corporate entity type suffix incompatible with a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation
Number-only names, extremely obscene phrases, or phrases that infringe protected trademarks (subject to Registry trademark check)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registered agent (or applicant) may request a written reason from the Registry's Dirección General de Registro. Within 5 business days of rejection, a formal 'Recurso de Apelación' (administrative appeal) must be filed with the Director General of the Public Registry, paying the non-refundable administrative fee of approximately USD 60–100 (tariff per the Registry's 2016 fee schedule, law 18 of 2015). If the appeal is denied within the statutory 30-day resolution period, the applicant may file a 'Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa' before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within 2 months. Regardless of appeal status, a new name may be reserved immediately after initial rejection without prejudice to the appeal. No extension of the 30-day reservation window is available; re-application after expiry is treated as a new request with new fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the legal registered agent (Resident Agent) address if it is a physical office in Panama City, maintained by the licensed Registered Agent (law firm or corporate services provider). However, because the entity will manufacture ICU mechanical ventilators and engage in Life_Support_Hardware_Mfg, the Panamanian Revenue Service and Ministry of Commerce require proof of real operating substance in the jurisdiction of the production site (likely a foreign subsidiary or a separate operating company). A virtual office without any physical presence, personnel, or local purchasing activity will not sustain economic substance requirements under Panamanian territorial tax law. For a PIF acting as a holding/licensing vehicle for an overseas manufacturing subsidiary, the PIF's substance can be maintained solely through its registered agent in Panama if no manufacturing activity is conducted in Panama; for active trading of medical devices, a local branch with licensed premises is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% (above-average for a manufacturer of critical care medical devices because Panama Customs (SENAVEFRONT) and the Ministry of Commerce in conjunction with Minsa may verify physical premises to confirm the issuance of the Sanitary Operation License and to corroborate under-declared imports of semiconductor/turbine parts. Enhanced audits are triggered if the PIF is used actively for manufacturing rather than passive holding. Unannounced visits by the Municipal Physiognomy or Fire Department are common for any commercial address in Panama City; also the Ministry of Health performs on-site checks for medical device facilities.)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Panama Private Interest Foundation Incorporation Fee (Standard 'Two-Office' 10-Act Registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – per its official fee schedule (First Act, Edicto, revision, inscription).
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Ley 18 de 2015 and Registry Fee Schedule; payable in cashier's check or ACH to Registry; often bundled by registered agent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company Name Clearance Search and Online Filing (Nombre o Razon Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official online search fee of approximately USD 15–25 per name (non-refundable).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Foundation Charter (Draft of Public Deed) and ancillary documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Notary (Notaría Pública Tercera or other)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee schedule established by Article 754-767 of the Notary Law (Ley 3 de 2010); approximately USD 150 per signed protocol.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Agent Fees – first year (mandatory resident agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based annual fee (common range: USD 300–600) – includes provision of registered office address, storage of foundation records, routine filing of annual franchise tax if applicable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / Consular Legalization of foreign UBO and founder documents (passports, resolution, good standing certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in the country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs/designated authority) and Panamanian Consulate where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille fee of approximately USD 40–100 per document in most countries; Panamanian consular authentication fee ranges USD 40–150. Estimated for 3 documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary UBO declaration filing with the DGI (Beneficial Owner e-Form)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenues (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative cost recovery; no direct fee for e-filing; this line covers notarial signature of UBO form and DGI e-signature token system (approximately USD 50).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation International Sanctions / PEP Screening and AML Risk Assessment (per named UBO/Guardian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party screening software provider + Compliance Officer fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate: USD 15–30 per UBO per screening against OFAC/UN/EU + local lists; USD 40-60 manual review and record maintenance documentation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Draft and revision of Foundation Regulation (Reglamentación) and Suite of By-Laws, including UBO scheme and guardianship appointment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian Law Firm / Licensed attorney drafter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based professional fee (hourly or flat) – commonly 1.5–2 months of registered agent fee; flat fee for PIF with 1–2 beneficiaries and complex governance is USD 700–1200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation trademark / name conflict search in Panama Industrial Property Office (DIGERPI) as prudent clearance for medical device brand; not mandatory for foundation name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama DIGERPI (Dirección General del Registro de la Propiedad Industrial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published official search fee: approximately USD 75 (descriptiva) + USD 10 per additional class; plus attorney time USD 50.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translations and certifications (Spanish/English) of UBO documents and any foreign-language resolution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Translator accredited by Panamanian Ministry of Education
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Panama statutory tariff for certified translation: USD 0.50–0.90 per line; fee approximated for 3 documents of moderate length.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Emergency holding reserve for Registry objectional filings, postal/courier fees, and unforeseen amendments to foundation charter before inscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency of 10% of subtotal; covers administrative extensions, corrected signatures, and electronic notary platform unfamiliarity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Regime), as amended by Ley No. 16 de 2015; Articles 17-23 (constitution and endowment), Articles 38-49 (Foundation Council, resident agent and administration); complemented by the Public Registry fee and inscription regulations for foundations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public, accompanied by the Reglamento (Foundation Regulations), inscribed in the Private Interest Foundations register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Ley 25 de 1995 imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital; however, the Foundation must dedicate an initial endowment sufficient for its purpose. Registry practice requires declaring a minimum initial patrimony of US$10,000 (cash or in-kind) in the Foundation Charter. No escrow or immediate deposit rule applies; the endowment is accepted by the Foundation Council at the first meeting. Annual state tax (tasa única anual): US$150 for capital up to US$50,000; US$300 for capital from US$50,001 to US$100,000; US$400 for capital above US$100,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 — FIRST MEETING OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME] — [DATE]. The Council unanimously resolves: (1) to accept the Founder's initial endowment of US$10,000 as fully subscribed and to hold it as the Foundation's core patrimony under Law 25 of 1995; (2) to adopt the Foundation Charter and Regulations as governing instruments, establishing the registered office at the Resident Agent's address in Panama City; (3) to appoint [NAME] President, [NAME] Secretary and [NAME] Treasurer of the Council for a two-year term; (4) to authorize the President and Secretary to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and apply for all commercial, sanitary, and environmental permits required for ICU ventilator manufacturing; (5) to approve ancillary acts. Meeting adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit of Panama and licensed Panamanian attorney (Abogado Idóneo).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney. The attorney drafts the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and the Regulations (Reglamento), fixing the Foundation's name, exclusive purpose (manufacture of ICU mechanical ventilators), initial endowment, Foundation Council composition, resident agent clause and succession provisions. The Founder executes the Charter before the Notary Public, who certifies signatures and issues the notarized testimonio for registration.
required_dossiers: Initial endowment declaration and source of funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary or the attorney identifies legal deficiencies, execute a notarial clarification (aclaración) correcting the Charter text and re-notarize before proceeding to registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized testimonio of the Foundation Charter together with the Regulations to the Private Interest Foundation Section of the Public Registry. Pay the statutory registration fee (arancel) at the Registry cashier, obtain the entry control number, and track the inscription. The Registry verifies the foundation name, statutory compliance, and Resident Agent endorsement before issuing the inscription certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Attorney professional ID (carné) and authenticated power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues observations (observaciones), file a written clarification and execute a notarial correction within the stated term; re-file the corrected deed. If refused, appeal the decision to the Director of the Public Registry or seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certified inscription certificate and payment of first annual foundation tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (certified copies) and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through authorized collection channels.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the certified inscription certificate (certificado de inscripción) and a legalized copy of the registered Charter. Confirm the Resident Agent in office and register the official notification address. Pay the first annual foundation tax (tasa única anual) of US$150 (capital up to US$50,000) at the DGI-authorized bank or e-tax portal and retain the stamped receipt (sello) proving fiscal standing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Regularize any late tax payment by paying the applicable surcharges (recargos); rectify registration data through a nota de aclaración if the certificate contains errors, and request expedited reissuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal industrial license (Aviso de Operación) and tax registrations (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Rentas Municipales, and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for industrial activity, declaring the address, floor area and activity code ISIC 3250, and pay the municipal industria y comercio tax estimate to obtain the municipal operating certificate. Register the Foundation in the RUC under economic activity 3250 as a territorial-source taxpayer and obtain the fiscal operation certificate (certificado de operaciones).
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription of the Foundation
Legal representative and Resident Agent identification
Lease deed or title evidencing right over the manufacturing plant
RUC registration form and supporting annexes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a reparo (deficiency notice), adjust declared floor area or activity codes, pay any corrected municipal tax and penalties, and resubmit. For RUC denials, correct the validation errors identified by DGI and resubmit with attorney certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Health authorization: sanitary operating permit of the plant and sanitary registration of the ICU ventilator
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD), single health window (SUAM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the sanitary operating permit for the medical device manufacturing establishment and the medical device sanitary registration dossier (expediente) for the ICU invasive ventilator. Attach the ISO 13485 quality management system certificate, technical file, device labeling, international risk classification (Class II), and Good Manufacturing Practices evidence. Undergo the facility inspection scheduled by MINSA.
required_dossiers: Technical file of the ICU mechanical ventilator
Facility layout and assembly validation reports
Product labeling and instructions for use in Spanish
Power of attorney for health registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MINSA technical observations within the granted term (typically 10 to 30 business days) with corrective medical-technical submissions; if refused, request reconsideration or appeal before the competent health registration body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental diagnosis, fire safety certification and occupational/labor clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and Caja de Seguro Social (CSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Category I environmental diagnosis for the assembly plant and obtain the environmental resolution. Request the Fire Department technical inspection and Visto Bueno certificate for the production building. Register the occupational health and safety committee with MITRADEL and submit the workplace risk assessment. Enroll employees with CSS and obtain the employer registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Facility blueprints and environmental management plan
Fire safety systems description and inspection report
Employee list and CSS employer registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For environmental observations, implement the mitigation measures required by MiAMBIENTE and request re-evaluation if the activity is reclassified. For fire deficiencies, remedy inspection observations (exits, detectors, extinguishers) and request re-inspection. For labor shortfalls, correct workplace safety conditions before issuance of the clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección de Empresas e Industrias, jointly with the Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Rentas y Catastro for the municipal industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Municipal de Funcionamiento / Aviso de Operación Industrial, and Permiso Sanitario de Operación de Dispositivos Médicos (MINSA - DNFD).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I - Diagnóstico Ambiental (registration-level environmental diagnosis; no full EIA required for light medical device assembly operations).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the national effluent regulation (MiAMBIENTE - Reglamento de Aguas Residuales) with pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 200 mg/L and TSS ≤ 100 mg/L. VOC and particulate emissions from soldering and cleaning stations must be captured by local exhaust and kept within MITRADEL occupational exposure limits. Hazardous residues (electronic scrap, isopropyl alcohol waste, lithium battery cells) must be managed under Resolution AG-0447-2017 through a licensed waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire prevention and structural exit certification (Visto Bueno), municipal structural load and occupancy inspection of the production bay, MITRADEL occupational safety and health committee registration with workplace risk records, and CSS employer enrollment with accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Directorate-General of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – MEF), Republic of Panama; official taxpayer portal: 'e-Tax 2.0' (Sistema E-TAX 2.0) at https://e-tax.dgi.gob.pa; customs administration is a separate authority: National Customs Authority (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas – ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF, Law 25 of 1995): 1) inscribe the foundation charter with the Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público) and maintain an active resident agent; 2) file the DGI inscription application ('Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente') together with the Aviso de Operación when trading in movable goods; attach the registered charter, resident-agent acceptance and receipt for the statutory annual foundation fee (B/. 350); 3) after DGI Census validation, obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and electronic taxpayer certificate; 4) activate ITBMS and FEL e-invoicing in e-Tax 2.0 before invoicing the ICU ventilator sales; 5) register in the MICI Export Registry and the ANA exporter log; a purely passive asset-holding PIF can remain without RUC until commercial operations actually begin, limits apply regarding false inactivity declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box or general hybrid-mismatch election. Available elections: (a) PIF operates as a distinct 'patrimonio autónomo' separate from founder and beneficiaries; only Panamanian-source income is within the tax net; (b) inclusion in the mandatory informative 'Régimen de Transparencia Fiscal Internacional' (Law 254 of 2021) via Formulario 940 for non-Panamanian-source income, while Panamanian-source business profits remain taxable at the standard 25% corporate income tax rate; (c) election of the ITBMS small-taxpayer simplified regime (pequeño contribuyente) where annual gross turnover does not exceed B/. 36,000; (d) election of ANA/MICI 'Autorizado Exportador' status to apply simplified export zero-rating. Any re-characterization of foreign income as Panamanian-source by DGI would require exceptional anti-abuse analysis under Law 254.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto sobre la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios (Panama VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 per annum (36,000 Panamanian Balboas at 1:1 parity with the US Dollar) of gross income from taxable transfers of movable goods or provision of services; once this threshold is reached or exceeded, the PIF must be inscribed as an ITBMS registered taxpayer in its RUC and issue FEL electronic invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory DGI electronic invoicing under the 'Facturación Electrónica en Línea (FEL)' framework administered in e-Tax 2.0: all registered ITBMS taxpayers must transmit invoices in the national XML schema to DGI in near-real time for validation and digital stamping (sellado electrónico); each accepted invoice obtains a unique DGI authorization code embedded in a QR code; taxpayer software and APIs must be homologated after testing in the DGI sandbox and operate under a valid Panamanian certified electronic signature (firma electrónica issued by an accredited certification authority under AIG/Registro Público rules); export invoices must cite the ANA customs declaration number and are subject to DGI exit-validation checks.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to turbine-driven critical-care invasive ICU ventilators (HS 9018.90/9019.20) when: (i) goods physically depart from Panamanian territory under a valid ANA export declaration in the name of the exporting PIF or its contract manufacturer; (ii) the foreign buyer is non-resident and title/risk passes abroad under EXW/FOB/CIF INCOTERMS; (iii) the sale is recorded as zero-rated in the FEL e-invoice linked to the customs number; (iv) the exporter holds an active RUC with ITBMS registration; (v) proceeds are received in the Panamanian banking system (USD/PAB) from abroad within the 180-day export proceeds benchmark and traceable to the same sale; (vi) for sales to free zones or bonded re-export, equivalent zero-rating certificates (zona franca purchaser export proof) are retained; supporting documentation must be kept for the DGI limitation periods of 5–7 tax years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Mercancías / DUA) filed electronically in the ANA SINTAD system, specifying HS 9018.90/9019.20 and the ICU ventilator particulars
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of the goods from Panamanian territory
Commercial export invoice issued under FEL (electronic) with the 0% rate and DGI authorization code
Purchase Order / International Sales Contract with the foreign buyer stating INCOTERMS, quantity, unit price and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 credit advice from the receiving Panamanian bank evidencing foreign-currency/USD payment collection
Exporter Registry certificate (MICI – Viceministerio de Comercio Exterior) and ANA Export Log enrollment
Certificate of Origin (where a preferential trade instrument is claimed) and, if required by ANA/DGI, the sanitary or medical-device export clearance for the ventilator units
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit under Código Fiscal Articles 744–749 applies formal strictness to zero-rating evidence: incomplete or inconsistent export files are recharacterized as local taxable sales, generating 7% ITBMS plus moratory interest (interés de mora) and fines ranging from 10% to 200% of omitted tax depending on negligence or intent; refunded input VAT is retroactively clawed back with indexation and the exporter is suspended or removed from the RUC/e-invoicing registry; false declarations expose the PIF and its directors to the criminal tax-evasion offense (introduced by Ley 70 de 2019 into the Código Penal), carrying imprisonment of 2–5 years; ANA customs fraud proceedings under Ley 76 de 2019 impose confiscation of shipments and fines of 100%–300% of customs value; regulatory revocation by MICI/ANA and DGI disqualification follow health-sector medical-device violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: None — Panama is fully dollarized and has no central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking and financial system regulator, and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US dollar is legal tender and no separate national currency exists; there is no exchange control regime, no dual market, and no foreign-exchange approval requirement. Both current account (commercial trade, services, profit remittance) and capital account transactions are freely convertible. Profit remittances are unrestricted from a currency perspective, but fund outflows are subject to SBP AML/CTF reporting and Panama's territorial taxation rules; income sourced abroad is generally not taxed in Panama. Dividends and profit distributions made by Panamanian entities out of Panamanian-source income are subject to the applicable dividend tax at statutory rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; exporters may retain all receipts in USD or any foreign currency and deploy them without central bank approval. Compliance is limited to banking documentation and anti-money-laundering requirements for the underlying export transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for trade settlement and operating cash management
Operational Account for USD clearing, SWIFT wires, and commercial LC issuance
Capital Escrow Account for statutory foundation capital and government-related settlement accounts
Operational Account for cross-border receivables and payables and liquidity concentration
Cross-border USD account for trade finance and commercial LC negotiation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury rail but viable as a secondary collection channel for smaller buyer payments. Offshore digital EMI virtual accounts are not treated as Panamanian bank accounts and cannot clear Government LCs or obtain SBP licensed banking services. Any locally active fintech or electronic payment institution must hold a Panamanian license from the SBP and must ring-fence clients' funds through a local commercial bank guarantor; therefore, the PIF and its operating company should maintain core liquidity and vendor disbursement capacity in a licensed tier-1 local bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for the principal decision-maker, at least one relevant director, and the beneficial-owner or founder when opening a corporate or foundation account. SBP due diligence rules require identification and verification of natural persons; remote video onboarding is accepted by some private banks only for enhanced-relationship clients, but for a Private Interest Foundation with non-resident founders, most tier-1 banks require at least one in-person KYC interview in Panama, with remaining documents notarized and apostilled. Where proxy signatories are used, a certified power of attorney executed before a notary and legalized by the Panamanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs is required; the first signatory still needs biometric verification at the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation opacity and complex beneficial-ownership chain involving settlor, foundation council members, and beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized foundation charter and bylaws, due-register certificate issued by the Registro Público de Panamá, beneficial-ownership declaration identifying the settlor, members of the foundation council, and final beneficiaries, abbreviated balance sheet or capital certificate, source-of-wealth questionnaire, bank references, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose of the PIF in the ICU mechanical ventilator manufacturing business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-risk medical-device manufacturing and export of ICU mechanical ventilators to foreign public health systems and government buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturing license and healthcare product registry certificates from the Ministerio de Salud de Panamá where applicable, ISO 13485 certificate, CE or FDA qualification documentation where available, signed purchase contracts, proforma invoices, delivery framework agreements, end-user declarations, import permits from destination countries, export declarations, customs documentation, and evidence of export-value reporting obligations being met.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from the PIF or offshore parent into the Panamanian operating and trading company for pre-export component procurement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal capital contribution or shareholder loan agreement, notarized board resolutions of all parties, source-of-funds evidence from the remitting bank, bank statements for the most recent three to six months, signed or audited financial statements, explanation of investment rationale, confirmation that no bearer instruments are outstanding, and precise wire instructions with remitter name matching the account holder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound SWIFT wire patterns to multiple component suppliers and logistics providers across jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice and purchase order per disbursement, supplier KYC file including legal identity and beneficial owner, vendor bank account confirmation, sanctions and PEP screening clearance, product due diligence evidence where applicable, logistics documentation such as airway bill or bill of lading, project budget and payment schedule, and a board-approved treasury controls memo evidencing segregation of duties and anti-fraud controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 from the parent or foundation board treasury to the Panamanian operational account. Wire details must show the exact legal name of the PIF or operating entity as beneficiary, the US-based correspondent bank of the Panamanian receiving bank, the account number, and a clear payment purpose in field 70 such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION'. Panamanian law does not require a foreign-exchange purpose code because payments settle in USD, but the receiving SBP-regulated bank will require an internal commercial classification; provide supporting board resolution, source-of-funds declaration, and signed contribution agreement. For sub-injections from foreign related companies, include a group funding structure diagram and transfer-pricing documentation demonstrating arm's-length interest rates if the funds are treated as loans rather than equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier settlements, logistics payments, and general operating disbursements. Use SWIFT MT700 documentary credits or MT707 amendments when selling to public health ministries and sovereign buyers under Government LC structures. Panamanian banks may provide pre-shipment finance, export LC negotiation, and confirmation through their global correspondent network. For Panamanian public procurement, settlement occurs through Banco Nacional de Panamá or authorized payment mechanisms under the PanamaCompra framework; invoice discounting and forfaiting of accepted sovereign LC receivables is permissible where a first-class confirming bank is used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable foreign exchange forwards (NDFs) executed with a licensed Panamanian or international bank for non-USD currency exposures
Deliverable foreign exchange forwards for major convertible currencies through the bank's offshore or derivative desk
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) matching EUR or CHF procurement liabilities to USD revenue streams
Foreign exchange options (calls and puts) for hedging tender-related currency uncertainty
Auxiliary derivative instruments such as interest rate swaps and commodity price hedges permissible under SBP derivative authorization frameworks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legal Entity Franchise Tax / Annual Tax on Legal Entities (Impuesto Anual de las Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 – January 15 for the reduced USD 300 fee; January 16 – March 31 for the USD 350 late fee; final default cutoff is March 31 of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$50 automatic surcharge applied if payment is not made by January 15; after March 31, monthly statutory interest and additional penalties accrue; three consecutive years of non-payment trigger administrative strike-off from the Public Registry and loss of legal good-standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the close of each calendar fiscal year; for non-calendar fiscal years, no later than the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end. Filing is performed electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines based on the tax payable (minimum US$10) plus monthly statutory interest on unpaid tax; persistent delinquency may lead to fiscal embargo, judicial collection proceedings, and eventual administrative strike-off if combined with franchise-tax non-payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Panama's Income Tax Code, legal entities engaged in Panama-source activities with annual gross revenue at or above US$3,000,000, or designated as Grandes Contribuyentes by the DGI, must file audited financial statements with their annual income tax return. Private Interest Foundations conducting no Panama-sourced commercial activities have no mandatory statutory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; accounting books must be maintained in Spanish and conform to the Uniform System of Accounts prescribed by the Código Fiscal for taxable entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 129 of 2020 (as implemented), the Panama resident agent must obtain, maintain, and hold accurate and current ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) information. The Private Interest Foundation must annually reconfirm, in writing, the identity of the foundation founder, council members, and beneficiaries, and must notify the resident agent of any change within the statutory notice period (generally not exceeding 15 days after the change). The annual reconfirmation is evidenced by a signed certificate retained in the resident agent's client file; there is no public filing of the UBO register with the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Miembros del Consejo)
Minute Book of the Foundation Council (Libro de Actas del Consejo)
Beneficial Ownership Register (Registro de Beneficiario Final)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable income exceeding USD 50,000; 15% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial tax system: income sourced outside Panama is exempt from corporate income tax. Standard ICU ventilator manufacturing is taxed at the progressive 15%-25% schedule. Qualifying Multinational Headquarters (SEM) license holders may elect a 0% ISR rate for eligible services, and a production plant located in a designated special economic zone such as Panama Pacifico may benefit from reduced effective taxation, but such incentives are not presumed for this manufacturing scope.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 201 (Informe de Renta de Personas Jurídicas / Declaración de Renta) filed electronically through the DGI T@x Net e-filing portal (e-Tax 2.0 system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the filing and payment deadline is 31 March of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from Panamanian-source operations, including ICU ventilator sales under government letters of credit and Swift wire transfers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all invoiced sales attributable to Panama; segregate and document any proven foreign-source export revenue excluded under the territorial regime

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: imported components, direct labor, manufacturing overhead, and depreciation of production equipment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate import costs with customs entries and arm's length intercompany invoices to avoid transfer pricing adjustments by the DGI

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: sales, general, administrative, maintenance, licensing, and regulatory certification costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses attributable to Panamanian-source income are deductible; retain complete invoice records to satisfy DGI documentary requirements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before application of the statutory rate schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 15% on the first USD 50,000 and 25% on the excess; no reduction is available unless a qualifying special economic zone or SEM license is in force

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance income tax payments made during the tax year, creditable against the annual ISR liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that quarterly provisional payments were registered in the DGI system to avoid a 10% surcharge on the unpaid balance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing information return supporting intercompany purchase and royalty transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File where annual related-party transactions exceed the USD 250,000 threshold; maintain a Spanish-language Local File and a consolidated Master File

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid tax after the statutory deadline bears a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest of 1.5%; late or omitted filing triggers administrative fines under the Fiscal Code, attachment of bank accounts, and suspension of the taxpayer's Registro Único Tributario (RUC) status

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional tax payment voucher (Pago Provisional Trimestral) submitted through the DGI T@x Net electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Four quarterly installments due by the last business day of March, June, September, and December of each fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable income for the current fiscal year, generally based on the preceding year's tax return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident operated manufacturers must base estimates solely on Panamanian-source net income and adjust when actual operations materially deviate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of each quarterly installment, typically a percentage of the prior year's annual ISR
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure wire remittances reference the correct DGI tax obligation code and are funded before the quarterly deadline

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Omission or underpayment of quarterly installments triggers the 10% surcharge and 1.5% monthly interest on the shortfall, together with administrative fines; persistent non-payment authorizes the DGI to enroll the debt for forced collection and asset seizure

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid out of net profits already subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 20% where dividends are distributed from profits not previously subject to Panamanian tax, such as exempt or foreign-source earnings held by the PIF
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficiary must obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction, have it apostilled or legalized, and deliver it to the Panamanian withholding agent before distribution; the paying entity submits the TRC and treaty-residency forms to the DGI to apply the reduced rate at source. Where domestic law already exempts the income, the treaty rate operates as a ceiling and does not increase the domestic tax burden; any excess tax withheld is recoverable through the DGI refund procedure supported by Forms 201 and the TRC annexes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding is 0% on interest and royalties paid to non-residents under Panama's territorial tax principle; DTA treaties commonly cap source-country taxation at 5%-10% for royalties and 5%-10% for interest. Because Panama domestic law does not impose a source tax on these categories, treaty caps confirm non-taxation rather than introducing an additional levy.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 250,000 in annual related-party transactions (the Panamanian Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the USD, so the local statutory threshold is B/.250,000)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Executive Decree 266 of 2020) apply to entities engaged in 'relevant activities', including IP holding, headquarters, distribution, financing, shipping, and insurance. Manufacturing of ICU ventilators is not a designated relevant activity; however, the PIF's commercial operations must still be evidenced by physical premises, qualified staff, operational expenditure, and board decisions made in Panama. A pure asset-holding PIF with rented filing-office substance is exposed to ESR and AML challenge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and under-declaration of revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare Panamanian-source ICU ventilator sales, issuance of false sales reports, or omission of cash-equivalent LC receipts while claiming an offshore source for the income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the omitted ISR with a 10% surcharge, monthly interest of 1.5%, administrative penalties under the Fiscal Code, and criminal prosecution for evasión fiscal where the omission is intentional and material
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and resident agents who sign false declarations may have the corporate veil pierced for civil restitution of the unpaid tax; conviction can result in arrest warrants, travel bans, and imprisonment under Panama's criminal tax law

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company abuse / Private Interest Foundation misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the PIF as a bare legal title-holder of the ventilator manufacturing business with no employees, no premises, no bank operations conducted in Panama, and no independent management
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution of the foundation, denial or revocation of the PIF certificate and statutory manufacturing license, monetary fines under AML Law 23 of 2015, and debarment from government LC procurement processes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The founder, council members, and protector may each be held personally liable for wrongdoings committed through the foundation; travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal charges apply where the foundation is deemed a sham instrument for money laundering

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and false invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing imported ventilator components from a related supplier, booking artificial royalties to a related IP holding entity, or issuing inflated invoices to support government LC draws
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI arm's length adjustment of Panamanian-source taxable profit, recharacterization of the intercompany transaction, 10% surcharge, 1.5% monthly interest, and fines up to 100% of the tax deficiency where fraudulent documentation is found
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the false pricing or forged invoices are jointly and severally liable for the deficiency; involvement in forged LC documentation attracts criminal money-laundering liability and personal attachment of assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML violations on government payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Government LC or Swift wire proceeds without structured customer due diligence, ignoring adverse media on end-buyers, or concealing the beneficial ownership of the PIF from the banking correspondent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to USD 1,000,000, suspension of the entity's commercial license, mandatory closure of the bank account, and reporting to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) as a predicate money-laundering event
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent face personal criminal liability under Law 23 of 2015 for willful blindness; sanctions extend to restraint orders over personal assets, travel restrictions, and sentences that can reach 15 years' imprisonment for aggravated laundering
